blurb: A `@raw` route hands the handler its request body as untouched octets, buffered in memory up to a cap. With no cap there is no bound on that buffer, which is the denial of service request body limits exist to stop, so a raw route must have one: a `@limit(maxBody:)` on the handler, or a `limits { maxBody = … }` on the service.
summary: A `@raw` route has no request-body cap (no `@limit` and no service `limits`).
